source: MazeMap building 1014912 polygons (map/source/mazemap/) and the route graph of the venue package

frame.venue: x = metres east, y = metres north of geo_origin (SW corner of the building outline's bounding box), z = metres up; floor 1 at z = 0. Same frame as map/research-techno-plaza.json
frame.gltf: right-handed Y-up: X = x (east), Y = z (up), Z = -y (south). Venue (x, y, z) -> glTF (x, z, -y); glTF (X, Y, Z) -> venue (X, -Z, Y)

unity.note: Unity is left-handed Y-up. Both common importers, UnityGLTF (SchemaExtensions CoordinateSpaceConversionScale = (-1, 1, 1)) and glTFast 4+, mirror X on import.
unity.as imported (X mirrored): Unity position = (-x, z, -y): Unity +x is west, +z is south. RouteCameraFollower.cs uses this with Flip X ticked (its default)
unity.after rotating the imported root 180 deg: Unity position = (x, z, y): x east, y up, z north (untick Flip X on the follower)

gltf_nodes: one node per level named L1..L9 (node extras carry floor and z); one mesh primitive per material

floor.used_for: floor slab (top at z): room floors

corridor.used_for: corridor / lobby floor plate (z..z+0.02), polished light-to-mid grey terrazzo with fine 2-4 mm darker chips; the page adds a planar reflection on it

lift.used_for: lift box: plate, band, cap, brushed steel

lift_lintel.used_for: lift wall above its opening, dark frame

stairs.used_for: stair box: plate, band, cap, concrete

corridor_borrowed.used_for: translucent: corridor floor the route graph borrows from another floor (not in this floor's map data)

floor_bridged.used_for: translucent: floor strip under an edge bridging a gap in the corridor data

door_uncertain.used_for: translucent amber panel filling the opening of a door whose position was guessed (z+0.02..z+2.2)

ceiling.used_for: ceiling at z+3.0 (underside of the ceiling plate)

roof.used_for: top and edges of the ceiling plate: the dark roof where no floor is above

facade_glass.used_for: exterior walls z+0.9..z+3: blue-green tinted curtain wall with thin faint mullion lines (translucent through the texture)

facade_sill.used_for: exterior walls z..z+0.9: aluminium sill panel

frame_dark.used_for: dark door frames (jambs and head), flush with the wall, only where a room's own door, a lift or stair entry or an entrance cuts a real wall; none at zones, titled corridors, neighbours' walls or doors off any wall

glass_pane.used_for: tinted glass: side panels beside office / meeting room doors, balustrades at the atrium void

column.used_for: round columns at the atrium void (generic), plain mid light grey

downlight.used_for: recessed ceiling downlights over corridors every 3 m (emissive discs, generic)

skylight.used_for: skylight over the atrium void on the top void level (emissive)

palette.terrazzo: #a3a19e (texture-darkened, with a planar reflection in the page)

style.modelled_from_data: slabs, corridor plates, every wall, opening, lift and stair box, the atrium void (corridor hole of floors 3-5) and the exterior walls (floor outline)
style.generic_not_surveyed: mullion lines, terrazzo speckle, ceilings at 3.0 m and the roof, downlight positions, the four columns, door frames, glass side panels, balustrade design, skylight

void.note: the atrium circle from the corridor data; two lift shafts stand inside it (the lift tower) and the floor bridges to them stay, so the open void is the circle minus cores and bridges

levels.name: Level 2 (corridors and cores copied from floor 3)
Level 6 (corridors and cores copied from floor 5)

data_gaps: Floors 2 and 6 have no corridor polygons in MazeMap and floor 8 only fragments: the corridors the route graph borrows (2 from 3, 6 from 5, 8 adds 9) are drawn as a translucent plate (material corridor_borrowed); the slab there = floor outline + rooms + a 1 m strip under every graph edge
Floor 6 has no lift or stair polygons: floor 5's are copied (also what the route graph does)
Edges whose hint starts '(corridor data incomplete' bridge a gap in the corridor data: the floor strip under them is translucent (material floor_bridged)

Door nodes labelled 'door position guessed': their opening is filled with a translucent amber panel (material door_uncertain) and listed in uncertain_doors with the corridor-facing wall segment, for a dashed outline

Openings of kind 'crossing' are where the route graph passes through a drawn wall (mostly the borrowed corridors of floors 2, 6 and 8, and door stubs of rooms that do not touch a corridor): confirm on site

camera_paths.note: per walk edge, a polyline the camera follows at eye height keeping clearance_m from every wall face and stopping door_stop_m before a door; the page and route.json use it instead of the straight graph edge
